summary: A heartbeat monitor for cron jobs: each job pings a URL when it finishes, the monitor calls it late and then down when the pings stop, one chat message per state change, and a dashboard with a 24-hour histogram. Healthchecks.io itself is open source, so self-hosting it is the fuller answer; this is the 300-line version you understand completely.

stack.why: a ping is one INSERT; the loop is a timer
one file that never fails a ping because it is busy

stack.choice: A VPS separate from the jobs
stack.why: a monitor on the same host reports nothing when it dies

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: A chat webhook URL (Discord, Slack or Telegram)
prerequisites.why: Alerts go to a chat channel you already watch. A webhook URL is the only credential this needs.
prerequisites.get: Discord: Server settings > Integrations > Webhooks > New Webhook, copy the URL. Slack: create an app at api.slack.com/apps, enable Incoming Webhooks, add to a channel, copy the URL. Telegram: create a bot with @BotFather and use the bot token plus your chat id.
prerequisites.verify: curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"content":"test"}' <url> posts a message (Discord form; Slack uses a text field)

prerequisites.name: Your list of cron jobs with expected periods
prerequisites.why: Each check needs a period and a grace time; deciding them makes Phase 2 testable.
prerequisites.get: crontab -l on every machine; write down name, schedule and how late is too late.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address. The monitor must live somewhere other than the machines running the jobs.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: Stable ping URLs that survive a server move.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: PORT
env.where: Any free port; Caddy proxies to it.

env.name: SITE_URL
env.where: Public base URL printed in ping URLs.

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: Ping ingestion
phases.goal: Accept pings on the Healthchecks scheme so existing crontab snippets port unchanged.

steps.do: Create the project and the tables
steps.detail: checks (id uuid, name, period_seconds, grace_seconds, status, last_ping_at, last_started_at, last_duration_ms), pings (id, check_id, received_at, kind, exit_code, body), alerts (id, check_id, from_status, to_status, sent_at, delivered, error). UTC epoch milliseconds throughout.
commands: mkdir heartbeats && cd heartbeats && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Route GET, POST and HEAD on /ping/:uuid plus /start, /fail, /log and /:exit_code
steps.detail: 0 is success, 1-255 failure. Store at most 100 kB of body. Always answer 200 OK; unknown uuids 404.

steps.do: Add a small CLI to create a check for testing

check: curl -fsS to a real uuid prints OK and inserts one row
A 2 MB body stores exactly 100 kB and returns 200
A random uuid returns 404 without creating anything
traps: Never local-time strings for timestamps; the late maths breaks across DST.

phases.title: State machine
phases.goal: up, late, down, computed every 30 seconds, one alerts row per transition.

steps.do: Write the evaluation: up within period, late past period, down past period plus grace; fail pings flip down at once; new and paused never alert
Record transitions in alerts and durations from /start to success

check: Period 60 with grace 30 reads up, late at 61 s, down at 91 s
Exactly one alerts row per transition

phases.title: Alerting
phases.goal: One message per state change with retries that never stall the loop.

steps.do: Write the sender for ALERT_FORMAT and drain undelivered alerts after each loop
Retry three times with backoff, then record the error on the row

check: Taking a check down produces exactly one message
A webhook that 500s leaves an error on the row and the loop running

phases.title: Dashboard
phases.goal: Manage checks in the browser and see every job at a glance.

steps.do: Basic auth on /admin with CRUD and the ping URL plus a crontab line per check
A status dot, relative last ping and a 24-hour histogram as inline SVG

check: Create, edit, pause and delete work in the browser

phases.title: Hardening and deploy
phases.goal: Rate limits, retention, HTTPS, a real crontab.

steps.do: Rate limit /ping generously per IP; add /healthz and nightly retention
systemd unit, Caddy, one real crontab line, the README
steps.detail: README: the one-liner with && curl -fsS, the /start and /fail wrapper, the same-host warning, and a line that Healthchecks.io is open source if you outgrow this.

check: A real cron job on another machine shows up
The README reaches a monitored job

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the monitor itself is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: Heartbeat monitoring others could rely on, watched from a box that is not theirs, itself monitored and backed up.

operations.restore: Copy back; the dashboard lists every check.
operations.monitoring: An external check on /healthz from another provider.
operations.incident: If the monitor is down, jobs are unwatched not broken; restore and review the gap.

releaseGate: Runs on a different provider than the jobs
Soak test: one flapping and one stable check alert correctly

notIncluded: Teams, projects and the integrations catalogue.
Being off your infrastructure by itself: put it on a different box.
after: A second alert channel behind the Notifier interface
A read-only status page from the checks table
